section.title: Objective and Overview
section.para: ACE, or Advanced Composition Explorer, studies the Sun and is one of only a few spacecraft that resides at the Sun-Earth L1 Libration Point in a Lissajous Orbit that is quasi-periodic. This tutorial will show the method in which a spacecraft may be station kept at this point in space. Put simply, a number of orbits about the Libration point will be simulated, with each being corrected slightly by small maneuvers due to the unstable nature of Sun-Earth L1.
This walkthrough is self-contained. Create the resources and mission sequence below in a new mission.

Objective: Maintain an orbit about the Sun-Earth L1 Libration point by varying the VNB burn component perpendicular to the direction of travel. At each EarthSunL1CS Y = 0 crossing, target the EarthSunL1CS VX component to zero.
Assume:
A preexisting orbit with given initial conditions
A UTCGregorian Epoch of 09 Dec 2005 13:00:00.000
Find: The deltaV required perpendicular to the direction of travel at each Y = 0 crossing to meet the above objective

section.title: Creating and Configuring the Resource Tree
section.para: This section will outline exactly what resources are required to complete the mission outlined within this tutorial. One spacecraft, a single burn to control that spacecraft, and a simple propagator, will be needed. To better see and analyze the spacecraft's motions, we will also need several Plots/Reports, Variable Object, and Coordinate Systems.

listitem.para: Spacecraft: ACE
Burns: dV
Propagators: DefaultProp (modified)
Solar System: DefaultBC, ESL1
Solvers: DefaultDC
Plots/Reports: L1View, EarthSunRotView, ESL1Ephem
Variables: TotaldV, VX, VY, VZ, dVX, dVY, dVZ, I
Coordinate Systems: EarthSunL1CS, EarthSunRotCS
Spacecraft
Rename DefaultSC to ACE
Change the Epoch Format to UTCGregorian
Set the Epoch to 09 Dec 2005 13:00:00.000
Propagators
Change the Min Step Size to 9.999999999999999e-022
Change the Max Step Size to 86400
Change the Max Step Attempts to 100
Open DefaultProp_ForceModel under Force Models. Clear PrimaryBodies and set PointMasses to Sun, Earth, Luna before Apply; the two gravity selections are applied together. Keep Drag None and SRP Off.
Keep DefaultProp Type RungeKutta89, InitialStepSize 60, Accuracy 1e-11, and StopIfAccuracyIsViolated true.
Solar System
Add a Barycenter under Calculated Points named DefaultBC and select Sun and Earth as its Bodies.
Add a LibrationPoint under Calculated Points named ESL1. Set Primary to Sun, Secondary to Earth, and Point to L1.
Burns

Rename DefaultIB to dV if it exists. In a new Qt mission, use Add ImpulsiveBurn under Burns, name it dV, and retain the Local coordinate system, Earth origin, VNB axes, zero elements, and DecrementMass false.
Variables/Arrays/Strings

To create the necessary variables, insert this declaration into the script before BeginMissionSequence. Build the script, then return to the mission controls to build all commands. This literal declaration creates only the variables.
listitem.programlisting: Create Variable TotaldV VX VY VZ dVX dVY dVZ I;

listitem.para: Coordinate Systems
EarthSunL1CS
Add a new Coordinate System and name it EarthSunL1CS
Set the Origin to ESL1
Select ObjectReferenced for Axes. In Qt, open Advanced and Axes to set the dependent fields below. Click OK in the axes dialog, then Create in the parent dialog.
Change the Primary and Secondary Values to Sun and Earth, respectively. Set XAxis to R and ZAxis to N; leave YAxis blank so GMAT completes the right-handed frame.
EarthSunRotCS
Add a new Coordinate System and name it EarthSunRotCS. Keep Origin Earth.
Select ObjectReferenced for Axes. In Qt, open Advanced and Axes to set the dependent fields below. Click OK in the axes dialog, then Create in the parent dialog.
Change the Primary and Secondary Values to Sun and Earth, respectively. Set XAxis to R and ZAxis to N; leave YAxis blank so GMAT completes the right-handed frame.
Solvers
Create a Differential Corrector Object under Solvers > Boundary Value Solvers and name it DefaultDC
Use the current default settings: MaximumIterations 25, ForwardDifference, NewtonRaphson, ShowProgress true and ReportStyle Normal. Choose a report file in a writable output directory.

Rename DefaultOrbitView to L1View.
On L1View's Setup tab, keep Add as ACE, Earth. Retain the current View Point Offset [30000, 0, 0] and View Up Axis Z. Configure the remaining settings as follows.

section.title: Creating and Configuring the Mission Sequence
section.para: Now that we have all the resources at our disposal to complete this mission, we will go ahead and start building the mission tree. ACE's mission is fairly straight forward at the level we will be dealing with. As stated before, the primary goal here is to allow the spacecraft seven iterations, or half orbits, and at the beginning of each one, calculate the deltaV required in the perpendicular-to-travel direction. The target sets ACE.EarthSunL1CS.VX to zero at the ACE.EarthSunL1CS.Y = 0 crossing; it does not set all three velocity components to zero. The entire Mission Sequence is relatively short and is given below in its entirety.

This particular mission tree may be a bit more complex than those you have previously dealt with but it is only due to the several equations and reports that it looks more complicated than it actually is. This part of the tutorial will go through the mission sequence step by step and at the end you will have a functional setup.

In Qt, use Insert after or Append command in the Mission tree, then choose the command template. Fill the settings below before Apply; Apply validates the complete mission. Equation steps use the Assignment template's Destination and Expression fields. For For1, select I as the Index, Start 1, Step 1, and End 7 before Apply. Use Append inside branch to add commands inside For1 and Target1. Set Target1 to DefaultDC with SolveMode Solve and ExitMode SaveAndContinue before Apply. Resize a command panel or scroll its form to reach lower settings. After Apply, close that panel before inserting the next command. The images below show the older GUI; the typed settings are authoritative.

listitem.para: Delete the initial Propagate
Report1:
Append this to the Mission Sequence Folder
Set Report file to ESL1Ephem and replace the default Parameters list with the six state parameters below.
Add ACE.EarthSunL1CS.X, Y, Z, VX, VY, and VZ to the parameters list
Equation1: Set to TotaldV = 0
For1: Change the End parameter to 7
Target1: select DefaultDC, SolveMode Solve and ExitMode SaveAndContinue. Add the following commands inside the target.
Vary1
Select dV.Element3, the current field equivalent of the legacy dV.B alias. Retain Local/Earth/VNB axes on dV, zero other components, and mass decrement disabled.
Set the initial value to 0
Set the perturbation to 1e-5
Set the Lower to -0.1
Set the Upper to 0.1
Set the Max Step to 0.01
Equation2: Set as VX = ACE.VX
Equation3: Set as VY = ACE.VY
Equation4: Set as VZ = ACE.VZ
Maneuver1: Select dV and ACE.
Equation5: Set dVX = ACE.VX - VX
Equation6: Set dVY = ACE.VY - VY
Equation7: Set dVZ = ACE.VZ - VZ
Equation8: Set as TotaldV = TotaldV + sqrt( dVX^2 + dVY^2 + dVZ^2 )
Propagate1: Set stopping condition as ACE.EarthSunL1CS.Y = 0
Achieve1: Set the goal as ACE.EarthSunL1CS.VX = 0 with a tolerance of 1e-005
Propagate2: Select DefaultProp and ACE, with a stopping condition of ACE.ElapsedSecs = 12000. This short coast follows the accepted target sequence and precedes Report2.
Report2
Select ESL1Ephem and replace the default Parameters list with ACE.UTCGregorian followed by the six state parameters below.
Add ACE.EarthSunL1CS.X, Y, Z, VX, VY, and VZ to the parameters list

section.title: Running the Mission
section.para: Save the mission, then Run. All seven target sequences should converge. L1View shows the successive arcs around the Sun-Earth L1 point; EarthSunRotView also shows Luna's orbit. Use Latest to show the entire retained trajectory and Fit to frame it.

ESL1Ephem contains one initial state record and seven records with UTC epochs and state components. Report2 runs after the 12000-second coast, so its VX values need not remain within the target tolerance. Check target convergence in the solver panel or message output. Finally, reopen the saved mission and confirm the Vary, Achieve and Target settings before continuing.

If you look into the reports stored in the directory specified then you will find the various parameters that were saved. This information provides insight as to the movement of the ACE spacecraft over time, especially if you take to a more text based presentation of information, rather than a visual one.

By now you should understand not only how to setup the required objects for this mission such as the Barycenter, Libration Point, Coordinate System Objects, Reports, Variable Object, and different views for the OpenGL Plot Object, but also how to apply these to create an effective and well documented mission.
